question.text: Which of the following risks is UNIQUE to AIF investing and not typically associated with mutual fund investing?

answer.text: Illiquidity risk due to long lock-in periods and unlisted investments

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook contrasts traditional/open-ended mutual fund liquidity with alternative-investment illiquidity. Category I/II AIFs are close-ended and primarily illiquid, with investors often unable to exit until winding up and distributions are completed. Illiquidity is the distinguishing risk feature of AIFs versus mutual funds. The Trap: Market, interest-rate, and regulatory risk all affect mutual funds and AIFs. Only illiquidity, tied to the close-ended structure and unlisted holdings, is materially different for AIFs. Note: Illiquidity in Category I and II AIFs is structural: the close-ended form means investors typically realise value only as winding up and distributions occur. This is the risk feature that most clearly separates AIFs from mutual funds.
